subject: Post-call: EHR triage & embedding/rerank PoC — summary and next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — EHR triage PoC (streaming, func-calls, embeddings)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Anika. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Pain points you shared
- Clinician triage latency: current rules engine is too slow for real-time workflows during intake (~2.5s average response per record).
- High inference cost at scale — embeddings + rerank for long patient notes is expensive and brittle.
- Structured extraction inconsistencies: downstream systems require stable JSON fields and we see drift across notes.
- Security/data residency: PHI remains on-prem for older clinics; some regional sites require EU residency.

Goals we heard
1) Build a PoC that reduces average triage latency to <800ms for the hot-path (first-pass classification + short hypothesis answers).
2) Cut per-record inference cost by 40–60% via batching, prefix caching, and a lighter rerank model.
3) Deliver deterministic structured output (schema + confidence scores) for triage fields.
4) Validate on a de-identified dataset from two clinics within 4–6 weeks.

Integration / product fit notes
- SDK: we recommend using Redwood's streaming client (node/python) to receive token-level events and function-calling hooks for structured outputs. This will let you emit partial decisions quickly and complete full structured JSON as tokens arrive.
- Function calling: propose a 'triage_decision' func signature: {"patient_id","note_text","clinical_context"} -> {"triage_level","probabilities","structured_fields"}. We can share a reference proto.
- Embeddings/rerank: we suggest an embedding + lightweight reranker flow — embed full notes with our quantized model for speed, then run a 2-stage rerank (cheap lexical + small transformer reranker) to improve precision on the high-risk class.
- Streaming & KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated clinician prompts (saves tokens) and continuous batching with 50–150ms dispatch windows.

Risks & open questions
- Data: need confirmation on de-ID process and size of sample (suggest 5k de-identified notes initially).
- Residency: clarify which clinics require EU on-prem or VPC deployment vs. hosted.
- Evaluation: what acceptance thresholds besides latency/cost (e.g., F1 for high-risk detection)?

Proposed next steps (timeline in parentheses)
1) Share PoC proposal and technical annex — attached (today).
2) Security intake: we’ll kick off the evidence checklist and a SOC/Security call with our security engineer (Ben) (this week).
3) Engineering deep-dive to confirm function signature, sample payloads, and SDK snippets (Nov 11–12).
4) Hand you a minimal evaluation harness and de-ID guidance; you return sample set (by Nov 20) so we can run initial metrics.

If that looks right, I’ll:
- Book the engineering deep-dive (30–45m) for Nov 11–12 — Marissa will propose times.
- Share the PoC doc and a short sandbox token for test calls.

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-nexa-poc-proposal.pdf (12 pages), security-evidence-checklist.xlsx (form)

1) De-ID: we can provide a de-identified export for two pilot clinics (~6k notes) but we need Redwood's de-ID checklist to ensure consistency (please include acceptable tokenization rules).

Hi Anika / Logan — quick technical clarifications from our end to prep the deep-dive: 

1) Function signature: we’ll propose a minimal JSON-RPC-like wrapper for the triage_decision call. Ben's straw-man:
- Input: patient_id (string), note_text (string, UTF-8), previous_kv_keys (optional list), clinical_context (map)
- Output: triage_level (enum), schema_version (string), structured_fields (array of {field_name,value,confidence})

2) Streaming: We'll stream progressive partials for two reasons — early triage and incremental structured extraction. The SDK event model supports: token.partial, func.invoke, func.result. That lets you render a UI decision before the full pass completes.

3) Embeddings & rerank: For speed we recommend: 1) chunk long notes into 512-token windows using our light tokenizer; 2) run dense embed with the quantized 8-bit model; 3) index with approximate nearest neighbor; 4) apply a tiny transformer reranker (2–4 layers) only on top 10 candidates. This usually gives 2–4% absolute uplift on precision with modest cost.

4) EU residency: For Clinic B we can offer a VPC-hosted inference path (customer-managed keys) and a short-term hosted option if you need it quickly — we’ll detail tradeoffs in the annex.

5) Data/sample: send a small sample (100 de-id notes) ahead of the deep-dive so we can validate tokenizer/chunking assumptions.

I’ll attach a short tech annex with code snippets and the func signature draft.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tech-annex-triage-snippets.md
